edit.description: The lock's `<name>(<args>)` wire-label grammar is split three times in this one file: `unit_shape_from_label` (795) at 802 and `registration_from_label` (1071) at 1079 each spell the same `label.strip_suffix(')')?.split_once('(')?` line, and `entry_shape_from_label` (966) re-implements it twice more on magic byte offsets — `label[7..label.len() - 1]` under `starts_with("scalar(")` (969) and `label[12..label.len() - 1]` under `starts_with("group-array(")` (976), each offset a hand-counted copy of its own literal's length. Fold all four onto one private helper beside them (`fn call_label(label: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)>`, the documented grammar's one reader), then match on the name it returns: `named-field`, the four field-carrying `Registration` channels, and `scalar`/`group-array`. The split is the only shared step — `entry_shape_from_label` keeps its own `member_key;lifted_fields` argument parse, and the bare-name vocabularies (`format_from_label` 782, `commitment_from_label` 811, `content_shape_from_label` 901, `collection_key_path_from_label` 1010) carry no call syntax and stay untouched. Behavior-neutral by construction: the two spellings already agree on every label, including nested parens and an empty argument. The two doc comments that today name the shared grammar in prose (792's "the same `<name>(<field>)` call syntax `registration_from_label`'s field-carrying variants use", 1067's "a `<name>(<field>)` call for the four field-carrying variants") shrink to a pointer at the helper — narration promoted to the surface that now holds it (`engineering.md`, "Narration is the ladder's bottom rung").

summary: The lock's `<name>(<args>)` label grammar has three decoders in src/kind.rs — one of them on magic byte offsets; they fold onto one split helper.

tests.asserts: one pin over the folded helper: each call-syntax family decodes through it (`named-field(name)`, `description-trigger(description)`, `enablement(enabled)`, `paths-match(paths)`, `event(event)`, `scalar(enabled)`, `group-array(hooks;matcher)`), and the labels the pre-fold spellings rejected still reject — a bare `named-field`/`scalar` with no call, an unterminated `scalar(a`, an empty argument `scalar()`, an empty `group-array()`, and a call on a name outside the vocabulary (`object(x)`)

the row-lift suite passes unchanged — `group-array(hooks;matcher)`, `group-array(hooks;matcher,timeout)` and `named-field(name)` still lift to the same typed facts, the fold's one behavior proof from outside the module

acceptance: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all --check and the rustdoc gate green; `rg -F "strip_suffix(')')" src/` returns the one helper, and no byte-offset slice of a label literal survives in src/kind.rs.
notes: Posture sweep, kind.rs neighborhood; three split sites, two spellings, one documented grammar, all verified on disk this tick. The SDK's encode side stays as it is: `declarations.ts` 264 and `builtins.ts` 560 interpolate the grammar at two kind declarations rather than decode it, and `builtin_lock_frozen` already drives that writer through this reader. scoped at dc51e31a
